extracted.intended_audience: film critics, aspiring reviewers, and anyone writing negative reviews of movies/books/meals/etc.
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on how to write fair, effective, and ethical negative reviews—how to ground complaints, acknowledge merit, judge works against their aims, and avoid mean-spirited invective. Primarily applied to film criticism but applicable to other review contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respond to something in the work
rubrics_metrics.description: "Are you responding to something in the movie, on some level? ... Is there something that I respond to and something that other people might respond to?"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for elements that genuinely elicit a reaction; it's possible to overlook flaws if something else in the work is working for you. A valid negative review should be grounded in an actual response to the piece rather than abstract invective.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid absolutism / hard rules
rubrics_metrics.description: "When we get into absolutism, I think that becomes a problem in film criticism, because if you have some sort of hard rule about what defines a good movie or a bad movie, you might end up bending your opinion on a movie just to match that standard."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not impose rigid, one-size-fits-all standards; allow nuance and let the individual work be judged on its own terms rather than forced into a predetermined checklist.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support complaints with specifics
rubrics_metrics.description: "Right. And that’s why I don’t like it when someone just says, 'Well, this movie was bad.' ... You have to support your arguments."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Back up criticisms with concrete examples and clear explanations of what bothers you. Avoid vague one-liners; provide evidence and reasoning so readers understand the basis of the negative judgment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be fair and acknowledge what the work is doing
rubrics_metrics.description: "Be fair if you can be. I think try to acknowledge what a movie’s doing."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even in a pan, credit what the work attempts or achieves (e.g., technical accomplishments, effective moments). Fairness includes noting both failures and any successes rather than only piling on negatives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluate the work against its artistic aims
rubrics_metrics.description: "Ask what is this thing trying to accomplish artistically, and through that lens, how well does it do it?"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify the work's intentions or ambitions and judge execution relative to those goals. Both the ambition and how well it is realized should factor into your assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treat unclear or offensive ambition as a substantive flaw
rubrics_metrics.description: "If you truly can’t tell what they’re trying to accomplish artistically, I think that’s probably a bad sign."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a work's aims are indiscernible, that lack of clarity is itself a legitimate point of criticism; likewise, if the work's ambition is offensive, note and evaluate that aspect explicitly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Credit technical or working elements even in negative reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Example given: acknowledging "an enormous technical achievement" or liking small elements such as particular characters even while disliking the whole.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Point out technical achievements or effective moments (acting, design, cinematography) so the critique is balanced and precise rather than blanket dismissal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid mean-spirited invective; maintain an ethical tone
rubrics_metrics.description: "There is an art to penning a pan—and maybe a code of conduct the critic should follow, lest scathing analysis shade into mean-spirited invective."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep criticism focused on the work, not personal attacks. Scathing language can be entertaining but should not devolve into cruelty or ad hominem remarks; maintain professional and ethical standards.
